title: Declarative release locks and resolution projections for model pins
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: customers need deterministic, auditable semantics for pinning models from the catalog across environments. Current ad-hoc pinning (tag string, free-form semver, or commit-ish) causes ambiguity at resolution time and makes rollbacks/fallbacks brittle. We must define a declarative lock construct and a deterministic server-side resolver that maps pins to immutable artifacts and performance profile snapshots.
background: We onboard many community and partner models. Each model has: a catalog id, a stream of builds / commits, semantic release tags, semver-style releases, and published performance_profile snapshots (e.g., perf-v1, perf-v1.1). Operators want to pin by tag (e.g., "stable"), semver ranges (e.g., ^1.2.0), or exact commit hash. The runtime must: 1) resolve pins consistently across SDK/server versions, 2) produce an immutable artifact id for runtime routing, 3) attach the intended performance_profile version to the resolution, and 4) support safe rollbacks and auditing.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a first-class "declarative_lock" binding customers can attach to their routes and SDK calls. Declarative locks contain three canonical selectors: tag, semver, commit. The resolver will evaluate selectors in a defined precedence order, emit a deterministic resolved_artifact_id and performance_profile_id, and record a resolution_snapshot in the audit log. SDKs will expose client-side validation and a light-weight 'resolve-preview' call for CI checks.
acceptance_criteria: Add API: POST /pins/resolve-preview that accepts a declarative_lock payload and returns resolved_artifact_id (immutable), performance_profile_id, resolver_version, and diagnostics (warnings).
Server-side resolver implements precedence: exact commit hash > semver exact match > semver range > explicit tag > latest. Precedence and tie-breaking must be documented.

Runtime will accept either explicit 'performance_profile' or 'performance_profile_selector' in the lock. If omitted, resolver attaches the latest compatible profile and returns the chosen profile id in the preview and resolution result.
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) have a new Pin API that serializes declarative_lock and surface 'previewResolution()' as a convenience for CI/CD.

System records a resolution_snapshot (timestamp, request_id, resolver_version, inputs, resolved_artifact_id, resolved_profile) in the existing audit log stream for every resolution and on each rollout change.
Backward compatibility tests: existing simple pin strings continue to work; resolver emits a deprecation warning if client sets ambiguous free-form pin that could match multiple selectors.

E2E test coverage across 5 model types (encoder-only, decoder-only, chat-style, 8-bit quantized, and fused-attention variants) validating that performance_profile_id selected matches profiler baseline within ±5% of token latency in staging.
Documentation and SDK changelog entries published in docs.redwood.ai/pinning and linked from Console pin UI by release time.
Rollout gating: feature flag controlled (pin-resolver-v2) and enabled for 10% of hosted API tenants initially.
implementation_notes: Resolver component: implement deterministic evaluation with compile-time selector graph. Keep resolver_version in semver and embed in audit exports.
Data model: add 'resolution_snapshot' table: columns as strings only for audit export: timestamp, request_id, input_pin_string, resolved_artifact_id, resolved_profile_id, resolver_version, notes.

Performance profiles must be versioned like 'perf:v1', 'perf:v1+gitsha'. When a semantic selector resolves to a model build, the resolver chooses the highest-profile version compatible with the artifact and writes the profile id in the snapshot.

SDKs: introduce 'DeclarativeLock' typed object. Do client validation locally (semver parsing, commit-hash regex) and expose warnings. Do not rely on client to resolve — always call server for authoritative mapping.
Console: add a 'Preview resolution' button on model pin configuration; show resolved artifact and perf profile and a diff compared to previously pinned artifact.

Fallback policy: allow customers to configure 'fallback_chain' which is a list of compatible selectors used when primary resolution fails because of compatibility. Default chain: same-model-minor-version -> compatible-quantized-variant -> last-known-good-artifact.
Metricing: add resolver.latency, resolver.miss_rate, resolver.fallback_rate. Emit tags: selector_kind and tenant_id.
Migration: when pin-resolver-v2 is enabled, run a backfill of top-10k frequently-used routes to record a resolution_snapshot for initial state.
Security: lock down the preview endpoint to authenticated service tokens only; previews should not leak internal model commit metadata to unauthorized tenants.

Edge-cases: if semver range matches multiple active artifacts with equal precedence, pick highest patch then highest commit timestamp; emit a 'non-deterministic-match' warning in diagnostics if two artifacts are equally recent and identical semver.

testing_notes: Unit tests: semver parsing, tag lookup, commit-hash exact matching, tie-breaking heuristics.
Integration tests: resolves across model variants and confirms resolver returns the attached performance_profile_id; run against staging catalog snapshot (catalog-2026-02-28).
Load test: exercise resolve-preview against 2000 concurrent requests to validate resolver.latency SLO < 50ms p95. If miss_rate > 1%, flag and investigate caching layer.
E2E perf validation: after resolution, run a short perf-runner job that emits latency metrics and verifies chosen perf profile is within expected bounds.
Rollback tests: simulate a bad profile being attached to a model and validate fallback_chain restores serving to previous artifact without traffic loss.
CAUTION: preview results are not authoritative for runtime routing; runtime always re-resolves at call time unless route has 'freeze_resolution: true'. Add tests for frozen routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable pin-resolver-v2 for 10% tenants. Monitor resolver.fallback_rate and model-serving error rates for 48 hours.
Phase 2 (expand): 50% tenants after no regressions in 7 days. Start backfill of popular routes.
Phase 3 (GA): 100% tenants and deprecate ambiguous free-form pin behavior with warnings in SDKs for one release cycle.
Communication: post release notes, docs page, and migration guide. Notify enterprise customers with dedicated migration window.
Rollback: feature flag off reverts resolver to v1 behavior; ensure audit snapshots remain queryable for troubleshooting.
